summary: High Society is a fast, brutal Knizia bidding game where players spend cash cards to win luxury items, except the player with the least money left at the end is disqualified from winning entirely. It plays in about 20 minutes but demands sharp psychological reads on when to bid, when to fold, and when to bail using the one escape card.
praised: quick, tense, and easy to teach
clever last-place-elimination twist forces careful spending
great psychological bluffing and bidding tension
small box, big impact for filler slot
criticised: can feel purely mathematical/dry to some
luck of card order affects available bidding options
one bad early bid can tank a player's whole game

interaction.detail: Every card auctioned is fully shared and visible, and players directly outbid one another in real time, watching rivals' remaining cash to judge how hard to push. There's no private tableau at all — the entire game state is the shared auction and each player's dwindling hand of money.

sources: total point value of won status cards, times multiplier cards, minus penalty cards
scoring.how_you_win: When the status-card deck runs out, the player with the highest total card value wins — but anyone left with the least money remaining is disqualified regardless of their points.
